biography: Peter Zbinden, born in the shadow of the Swiss Alps, didn't discover racing through karting like most. His passion ignited watching grainy VHS tapes of Group C endurance races with his grandfather, a former mechanic. Instead of simulators, Peter honed his skills blasting down mountain passes in his beat-up VW Golf, learning car control the hard way. He scraped together enough francs to enter a local Porsche Club race in 2020, stunning everyone by taking pole position in a borrowed 911 RSR. Now, at 27, Zbinden is at his peak, a terror on the European historic racing scene, driving a meticulously restored Porsche 911 RSR 74. Though he has never driven modern machinery, his prowess in classic sports cars is undeniable, and he is constantly seeking to improve his race craft. He dreams of one day racing at Le Mans Classic.
drivingStyle: Zbinden's driving style is all aggression and controlled chaos. He attacks every corner with a ferocity that borders on reckless, often throwing the car in sideways and relying on his uncanny car control to pull it back. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and his willingness to trade paint. While his tire management could use some work, his raw speed and relentless pressure on his opponents make him a formidable competitor, particularly in shorter sprint races.

rivalries.reason: Dubois, a veteran of historic racing, accuses Zbinden of being overly aggressive and disrespectful to the history of the sport. The two have clashed on track multiple times, resulting in damaged cars and heated exchanges in the paddock.

Rossi, a rising star in historic racing, is often seen as Zbinden's equal in terms of raw speed. Their battles are always close and exciting, with each driver pushing the other to the limit. There is a growing respect between the two, but that hasn't stopped them from engaging in some intense on-track duels.

Richter, a wealthy gentleman racer, is often frustrated by Zbinden's aggressive tactics. Richter believes that historic racing should be about preserving the cars, not risking them in unnecessary battles. Zbinden, on the other hand, sees Richter as a slow and predictable obstacle.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky wristwatch his grandfather gave him before every race.
Listens to vintage Swiss folk music on his headphones before getting into the car.
Refuses to wash his racing suit, claiming it retains the 'essence of speed'.
famousQuote: If you're not on the edge, you're taking up too much space.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2023 Spa Six Hours in his Porsche 911 RSR, battling through torrential rain and a failing gearbox to take the checkered flag.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Goodwood Revival in 2022 after a collision with Jean-Pierre Dubois, resulting in significant damage to his beloved Porsche.
